title_original: Art Basel Hong Kong Reveals 2027 Exhibitors and Program
excerpt_original: The forthcoming edition will present 232 galleries from over 40 countries and territories, and a citywide public program. The Editors

blocks.text: Art Basel Hong Kong Reveals 2027 Exhibitors and Program

blocks.alt: Art Basel Hong Kong Reveals 2027 Exhibitors and Program

blocks.text: Art Basel Hong Kong (ABHK) has unveiled the exhibitor lineup and program for its 2027 exhibition, which will take place from March 25–27 at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre (HKCEC), with preview days on March 23–24.

ABHK will gather 232 galleries from over 40 countries and territories—slightly down from its previous iteration—including 31 first-timers from Greater China, Japan, South Korea, Thailand, Europe, and North America. Among the majority of participants who maintain a presence in the Asia Pacific region, 27 are from Hong Kong, including Alisan Fine Arts, Blindspot Gallery, Empty Gallery, gdm, Kiang Malingue, and Rossi & Rossi.

Notably, the 2027 edition will introduce a new floor plan, moving its special sectors and curated presentations—Discoveries, Insights, Echoes, and Zero 10—to Level 3 of HKCEC. The revamped layout will give the sectors more floor space and visibility, according to the fair.

The main Galleries sector will feature 171 exhibitors, with 31 first-timers from abroad, including Galerie Nordenhake, Richard Saltoun Gallery, Matthew Brown, and Emalin. Among the 32 galleries hailing from Mainland China are BANK, Beijing Commune, and Magician Space, while the 20 galleries from Japan include Misako & Rosen, Taka Ishii Gallery, and Tomio Koyama Gallery. From South Korea, returning exhibitors include Arario Gallery, Gallery Baton, Kukje Gallery, and PKM Gallery. As Taiwan brings together eight participants—Lin & Lin Gallery, Mind Set Art Center, and Tina Keng Gallery and TKG+—those joining from Australia, New Zealand, and Southeast Asia comprise Richard Koh Fine Art, Silverlens, Starkwhite, STPI, and Sullivan+Strumpf, among others.

While five galleries are returning after a hiatus—Vadehra Art Gallery, Marian Goodman Gallery, Goodman Gallery, Alfonso Artiaco, Galerie Vazieux—several others who participated in the last year’s fair will sit out the forthcoming edition: DE SARTHE, Mennour, Josh Lilley, Richard Nagy, Tang Contemporary Art, and Pace Prints.

ABHK will also stage Echoes and Zero 10—two sectors that debuted last year at the fair. Echoes will showcase works produced within the past five years through 15 curated presentations by 18 galleries, including Neon Parc, Yeo Workshop, and Double Q Gallery. Zero 10, dedicated to digital art, will be helmed by independent curator Sunny Cheung, formerly the curator of design and architecture at Hong Kong’s M+.

In the Discoveries sector, 25 galleries will mount solo booths spotlighting emerging artists whose works center on the human body, materiality, and domestic life. Meanwhile, the large-scale installations, sculptures, and performances in the fair’s Encounters sector will again be overseen by a curatorial team led by Mami Kataoka with Isabella Tam, Alia Swastika, and Hirokazu Tokuyama.

Beyond the convention center, ABHK will present a citywide public program. The fair will provide free public access to the Film sector, curated again by Hong Kong video art pioneer Ellen Pau, and organize various initiatives with local institutions such as M+ and Tai Kwun.

In a press release, ABHK director Angelle Siyang-Le commented: “The most important and innovative dialogues emerge at the intersection of different worlds, where artistic, cultural, and business communities come together to generate new ideas, perspectives, and opportunities for exchange. As Asia continues to shape the global cultural landscape, [ABHK] provides a platform for these connections to flourish.”
